description_json.name: ROT-13
description_json.idea: A fixed monoalphabetic substitution over the English alphabet using a Caesar shift of 13. Each plaintext letter is replaced by the letter 13 positions later in the alphabet, wrapping around at the end. The mapping is the same for uppercase and lowercase letters. Non-letter characters are left unchanged. Because applying a shift of 13 twice over a 26-letter alphabet restores the original text, ROT-13 is self-inverse.
description_json.encrypt_rules: Use the following bijection: plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz -> ciphertext alphabet nopqrstuvwxyzabcdefghijklm. Thus a->n, b->o, c->p, d->q, e->r, f->s, g->t, h->u, i->v, j->w, k->x, l->y, m->z, n->a, o->b, p->c, q->d, r->e, s->f, t->g, u->h, v->i, w->j, x->k, y->l, z->m. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules: Apply the same ROT-13 mapping used for encryption. Since every letter is shifted by 13 positions in a 26-letter alphabet, applying the transformation twice restores the original letter. Thus n->a, o->b, p->c, q->d, r->e, s->f, t->g, u->h, v->i, w->j, x->k, y->l, z->m, a->n, b->o, c->p, d->q, e->r, f->s, g->t, h->u, i->v, j->w, k->x, l->y, m->z. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
